newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
TELECOMMUNICATIONS STRIKE CONTINUES

A strike by more than one million telecommunication employees over a bonus issue is threatening to snowball. Striking unions and the government hardened their stances. The workers' federations have threatened an indefinite hunger strike from October 26, 1996.
Indian Express
APEX COURT CALLS FOR REMOVING INDUSTRIES OUT OF DELHI

The Supreme Court has asked the Delhi government to create a new industrial belt outside the National Capital Region. The court set a 14-day deadline before which the Delhi government must relocate 39,000 industries away from the residential areas in the capital. The court has pre-empted any possible judicial review of its decision. The Supreme Court's move is aimed at driving the hazardous industries upsetting the capital's ecological balance.
The Economic Times
IDBI SEEN OFFERING 15 PCT COUPON

The Industrial Development Bank of India's (IDBI) planned 10 billion rupee bond issue is likely to offer a 15 percent coupon for investors. The new coupon rate will be 1.5 percentage points lower than the one on its earlier 16.5 percent offer on Super Deposit Bond 1996 and Growing Capital Bond 1996. The IDBI's decision to reduce the coupon rate was based on expectations of a general softening of interest rates in the post-credit policy scenario, said sources.
MULTINATIONALS KEEN ON RAILWAY WAGON LEASING DEAL

Multinationals (MNCs) and domestic financial institutions (FIs) are ready to pump in 15 billion rupees in leasing rolling stock to the Indian Railways if the own-your-wagon scheme is amended. These MNCs and FIs have demanded a 18 percent rate return along with depreciation allowances on their investment. U.S. based General Electric is willing to fund leasing of a minimum of 15,000 wagons provided the scheme of leasing wagons from the private sector is amended. Tata Lease Finance Company has offered to lease wagons worth two billion rupees on above terms. The Railways are said to be working out a formula to incorporate these demands.
Financial Express
ENERGY SECTOR NEEDS AT LEAST $1OO-BILLION INVESTMENT

The government has prepared a paper on reforms being carried out on the economic front. Titled "India Country Report", the paper will be presented at next week's infrastructure meeting in New Delhi. According to the report, India will need an investment of $100 billion to develop its energy sector. The report gives a clear picture of developments in various sectors and the role the private and public sector will play in the liberalised scenario. It enlists the investment opportunities available in the power, telecommunications, electronics, transport, oil and natural gas sectors. The paper says per capita consumption of energy in India may increase by 145 percent by the year 2010. For this, the required investment may be between $100 billion and $150 billion in the next 10 to 15 years.
STOCK MARKETS IN BEAR GRIP , DOWN 90 POINTS

An upswing in equities was halted on the stock exchange on Thursday, with pivotal stocks surrendering most of the previous day's gains on the lack of follow-up support, coupled with bear hammering. After gaining 200 points in the last two sessions, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sensitive index fell 90.92 points to 3250.94. It touched a day's low of 3241.15 in the session. The BSE-100 index dropped sharply by 32.14 points to 1447.86. The BSE recorded a turnover of 6.38 billion rupees.
STEPS TO REVIVE' SICK UNITS ASSURED

Labour Minister M Arunachalam has hinted at steps to revive the sick industrial units. Inaugurating the 33rd Indian Labour Conference in Delhi, the minister said the government had discussed with the Banking Department steps to remove industrial sickness and create a better alternative to Board of Industrial Finance and reconstruction, which would address the workers' needs. The conference is being attended by the representatives of five trade unions, employers and state governments and Union Territories. On the issue of child labour, the minister assured the government was committed to eliminating child labour from all occupations.
ESCORTS TIES UP WITH MAHLE

Escorts Ltd, flagship of the 30 billion rupee Escorts group, announced a 50-50 joint venture with its long-time technical collaborator, Mahle Gmbh of Germany. The joint venture company will manufacture automotive railway and gudgen pins. The new company would take on Escorts' manufacturing facilities at Bangalore and Patiala. It would also bring within its fold the pistons business of Goetze (India) Ltd, another Escorts group company which began in collaboration with Mahle.
BONUS CAP REMOVAL TO COST GOVERNMENT TWO BLN RUPEES

Removal of the ceiling on bonus may cost the Department of Telecommunications an additional two billion rupees, the communication ministry said. The railways ministry's decision to raise the ceiling on a bonus for railway workers has drawn flak from the government. Currently, telecommunication and postal workers are on a nationwide strike demanding bonus parity with their railway counterparts.
MINISTER TOUGHENS STAND ON TELECOMMUNICATION STIR

Communications Minister Beni Prasad Verma has hardened his stand against the one million striking non-gazetted employees of the telecom and postal departments. He ruled out negotiations until the indefinite strike was called off, even as the Regional Labour Commissioner initiated conciliation proceedings between the government and the striking unions. He said the ministry had chalked out alternate emergency measures but refused to elaborate.
STATE BANK SLASHES PRIME LENDING RATE

The State Bank of India (SBI) has cut its prime lending rate (PLR) by one percent to to 14.5 percent and introduced differential interest rates. This will be effective from November 1. The SBI introduced the differential rates by fixing the maximum spread over PLR fixed at 3.5 percent on demand loans and 3.75 percent on cash credits for all advances other than consumer credit. The maximum spread on term loans will be 3.5 percent. Following the SBI move, other banks have cut their PLRs.
FIAT ARM PLANS $1.5 MLN IRON VENTURE

The Italian-based Fiat group has drawn a comprehensive plan for its investments in India. Fiat group arm Teksid plans to set up a joint venture iron and aluminium foundry in India, with an estimated investment of $100 to $150 million. Teksid is the biggest foundry in Brazil. It produces aluminium castings and foundry presses and Snia and is also involved in biomedical and bioengineering industries. Teksid recorded an annual turnover of $1.2 billion in 1995. Another Fiat group company, New Holland, which manufactures tractors and agricultural machines, is also setting up a greenfield tractor plant in India.
Business Standard
SUGAR INDUSTRY SPLIT ON TOTAL DECONTROL

Differences between the private and the cooperative sector sugar units widened further with both taking divergent stands on crucial issues such as delicensing, export decanalisation and complete decontrol. While the private sector, represented by the Indian Sugar Mills Association, called for freeing all controls, leaders of the politically influential cooperative sugar sector favoured continuation of the present policies.
GOVERNMENT WANTS TO FIX MINIMUM DAILY WAGE AT 35 RUPEES

The government wants the floor-level minimum wage to be fixed at 35 rupees per day. It aims at gradually bringing the national labour policy in line with the common minimum programme detailed by the government when it came to power. The labour minister said priority would be given to preventing sickness and the revival of sick industrial units.
Business Line
POWER MINISTER ALLAYS FEARS OF U.S. INVESTORS

Power Minister S Venugopalachari, now visiting the United States, assured American investors that India's reform process was irreversible and sought foreign investment in the power sector. Addressing meetings with groups of investors in Washington, Houston and New York, he said the clearance of power projects had been simplified and decision-making steps reduced. He identified the transmission and distribution sectors as new areas in which foreign investment would be welcome.
